title: Takahashi EM-200 Temma II

html:
A few days ago, I went from a fork mount (the lx200's) to an equatorial mount.

I had two mounts in mind
1- The Astro-Physics Mach1 GTO
2- The Takahashi EM-200 Temma II

Given the availability on the used market, I bought a Takahashi EM-200 Temma II.

What a difference from the LX200's fork mount !!?!?!!?

First impressions.

1- Everything is super tight. It's Japanese
2- The polar scope is a marvel. Polar alignment takes 1 minute and the accuracy is good enough to do 5-minute subs without star trails at 400 mm focal length.
3- The periodic error is smooth and about +- 5 arcsec over 8 minutes.
4- The Temma II needs a computer to do the goto. I use TheSky 6 and it works very well. I'm waiting for a Skyfi so I can use my ipod touch as a wireless controller.
5- The instruction manual is pretty poor and the translation leaves something to be desired. Here we are far from the level of detail of the Astro-Physics manuals.
6- On 5-minute subs, I went from an fwhm of 4-9 to 2.20..... yeaaaaahhhh !!!

I'll do a more detailed review once I've had a few good photo sessions.
